facts.text: I have an ulcer on my tongue.

facts.item: how long the tongue pain, ulcer and painful swallowing have lasted
tongue pain, ulcer and painful swallowing: course

facts.text: Because of it I've become dehydrated.
Before the ulcer formed, my tongue turned blue.
Before coming here I was first treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
After that I was given acyclovir.
Along with the acyclovir I was given fluconazole.
None of those treatments improved my symptoms.

findings.name: oral examination
findings.result: Dry mucous membranes; well-demarcated area of necrosis involving the anterior one-third to one-half of the tongue, tender to palpation.

findings.name: CT angiogram of the head and neck
findings.result: Undulated-beaded appearance of the distal internal carotid arteries and vertebral arteries bilaterally.

findings.name: tongue biopsy
findings.result: Marked acute inflammation and granulation tissue with focal loss of the squamous mucosa; no fungal elements on staining; immunohistochemistry negative for cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex virus and varicella zoster virus.

aliases: giant cell arteritis with lingual necrosis
gold.reasoning: 1. Infectious causes were excluded—“No fungal elements were identified with staining, and no viruses…were identified with immunohistochemistry markers.” 2. Diffuse atherosclerosis was less likely—“the undulated-beaded appearance of the distal internal carotid and vertebral arteries bilaterally was more consistent with skip lesions occurring secondary to a vasculitic process than diffuse atherosclerosis.” 3. Other vasculitides were considered—“differential for tongue necrosis includes…other vasculitides such as granulomatosis with polyangiitis or polyarteritis nodosa.” 4. Giant cell arteritis was favored given epidemiology and rarity of lingual necrosis—“GCA is likely the most common cause of lingual necrosis when it does present.”

notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation after 2 weeks of worsening tongue pain, ulceration and painful swallowing (s001-s008).
The outpatient antimicrobials before the index visit (s004) are earlier treatments: one medication fact per drug, in order, plus one fact that none of them helped.
The duration and the worsening course apply to all three presenting complaints and are standalone facts.
